stories.title: My Dad Is in Prison. Here’s Why I Built an AI Chatbot for His Electronic Tablet.
stories.summary: CJ Jones built an AI chatbot for his incarcerated father, turning a personal need into a company called Beyond Bars AI. It's helping families stay connected and informed.
stories.extended_summary: CJ Jones, a technology analyst, created an AI chatbot named Nova for his father who is in prison. What started as a way to help his dad get answers has grown into Beyond Bars AI, a for-profit company. While the tool has limitations, it's a creative solution to the challenges of incarceration, offering support and information to families navigating the criminal-legal system.

stories.title: Startup Spotlight: Tech consultant returns to the farm with Reroot, connecting growers with consumers
stories.summary: Genevieve Priebe traded her tech consulting career for farming and built Reroot, a startup connecting local growers with consumers. Her app maps 50,000 producers, and her voice-powered tool lets farmers update their stores hands-free. It's a homecoming that's changing how we buy food.
stories.extended_summary: Genevieve Priebe used to advise Seattle's tech giants; now she bottle-feeds baby goats between business meetings. She's the solo founder of Reroot, a marketplace that makes local food as easy to buy as anything online. Her patent-pending Walk & Talk tool lets farmers update their stores by voice, even without cell service. It's a fourth-generation farm kid's dream, rebuilt for the digital age.

stories.title: Steven Jiang Is Teaching Kids to Question AI Before They Touch the Screen
stories.summary: Steven Jiang's Overture teaches kids AI literacy with paper-and-pencil lessons, no screens. The program, in 50+ schools, helps students spot AI mistakes and think critically before they ever touch a tool.
stories.extended_summary: Kids are already using AI, but few understand it. Steven Jiang is fixing that with Overture, an education company that teaches AI literacy in over 50 schools — using only paper and pencil. No dashboards, no prompt boxes, just critical thinking. 'Kids are growing up around AI but not getting a proper introduction to understanding it,' he says. The lessons help students spot mistakes and create with confidence, preparing them for a world where AI is everywhere. It's a screen-free approach to a digital future.
